Fact Extraction for Local Agent Memory: A 0.6B Model, Six Write Arms, and the Raw-Turn Trade-Off (2026)
Which Local Model Should Write Your Agent's Memories? Six Write Arms Measured on 8 Turns and 9 Facts (2026)
presentation.title_rationale: The selected title names the topic (agent memory fact extraction) and the constraint (0.6B local model) before the reader problem, then promises three things the matrix actually measures: dropped facts (0.5B arm recovered 3 of 9; P2 fragments), acknowledgement rows stored (1 of 12 vs 4 of 8 for raw turns) and what raw turns cost instead (73 vs 46 characters per top-5 prompt). It does not claim a 0.6B model cannot extract, because the run contradicts that.
presentation.long_title_reason: 131 characters. Three measured clauses are each backed by a separate column in results.json; truncating to 80 would delete at least one clause and imply a broader claim than the 8-turn fixture supports. Kept as the selection and research brief fix it.
presentation.visual_purpose: Horizontal bars per write arm showing characters in one top-5 prompt (retrieved rows summed, 365 raw turns vs 685 for the four-row two-turn window and 230 for qwen3:0.6b P1) and answerability@1, with each arm's acknowledgement rows over its own stored-row denominator (8/4/12/28/16/20). All values are results.json fields; nothing is invented, and the fixture scale and CPU-only host are stated on the image.
